correctness.rationale: Exact two-outcome truth-set analysis proves pure-line modal IA criterion; rectangular-support partition proves exact finite structural probability. Sparse Poisson thinning plus row/column collision bound proves the low window. Individual pure-line binomial law yields universal finite bounds and off-window regimes. Joint factorial moments over selected rows/columns converge to those of four independent Poisson variables in the upper critical window, yielding the exact squared formula. Near-complete Poisson missing-cell argument proves the stated gap. Exhaustive independent finite semantic checker validates all ternary game tables for m<=3 and rational structural probabilities.

value.rationale: The paper-facing mismatch between action-level independence and all-valuation modal-axiom validity is a natural logical and semantic gap. An exact pure-line criterion and two separated critical scales explain how the axiom becomes valid, invalid, then valid as independent action availability grows. Explicit sparse and upper-window limits and the nearly complete positive gap quantify a substantial structural phenomenon, rather than an arbitrary small numerical census.
